en: Sutta Nipāta 4.4 Suddhaṭṭhakasutta I see the pure, supreme, and healthy state;
A person’s purification comes through what has been seen;
knowing thus that this is supreme,
one attains the knowledge that "I am observing purity."
If a person’s purity comes through what is seen,
or if he abandons suffering through knowledge,
then that one who still possesses acquisitions is purified by something other [than the truth].
For views indeed lead him astray when he speaks thus:
"A brahmin does not say that purity comes from anything else—
neither from what is seen, heard, moral habits, vows, or what is sensed."
Unstained by merit or by evil, having abandoned the self and not forming anything here,
they have left the former behind and are intent upon the latter.
Those who follow after craving do not cross over attachment;
they grasp and let go, like a monkey letting go of one branch while grasping another.
A person who has undertaken various vows,
being bound by perceptions, goes from one state to another;
but the wise one, having fully understood the Dhamma through his knowledge, [remains steadfast].
The one of vast wisdom does not go from high to low.
Having become free from enmity toward all phenomena—
whatever is seen, heard, or sensed—
Who here in the world could form a conceptual construction about that very Seer who moves with his eyes open? They do not construct;
they do not hold him in esteem.
They do not say that ultimate purity lies therein;
having cast off the fetter of grasping and its entanglements,
they harbor no expectations for anything in the world.
The Brahmin has transcended the boundary;
for him there is nothing grasped through knowing or seeing.
He is neither one who lusts after passion, nor one who delights in the fading away of passion.
"For him, there is nothing here further to be grasped.
This is the fourth sutta, the Pure Octad.
